newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 22.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Wednesday's Daily Variety:
* Viacom Inc's Paramount Pictures and Cruise-Wagner have paid a low six-figure sum against a mid-six-figure sum for a science fiction film, Timejumpers, that might star Tom Cruise and Emilio Estevez.

* Senate Commerce Committee Chairman John McCain led a bipartisan group to introduce campaign finance reform legislation Tuesday that would require broadcasters to give free and discounted air time to federal political candidates.
* Bruce Willis has received an equity interest in L.A.-based Activision Inc and profit participation as well as a fee for his work on an upcoming vidgame, Apocalypse.

* The Directors Guild of America chose five first-time nominees for its feature film honors Tuesday -- Anthony Minghella for The English Patient, Joel Coen for Fargo, Cameron Crowe for Jerry Maguire, Mike Leigh for Secrets & Lies and Scott Hicks for Shine.
* Mayfair Entertainment has acquired all international rights to filmmaker Morgan Freeman's Hurricane for what sources estimate to be more than $1 million.
* About 600 people attended a second public hearing on Universal studio's 25-year plan to expand its lot. Universal Studios is 80 percent owned by Seagram Co Ltd.
